scenarios.title: The Fan Convention
scenarios.text: A fan convention wants you for a signing weekend. The line includes people who've followed you since high school, and one woman has your peewee league photo.

choices.label: Talk to every person
choices.result: Every person in line gets a real conversation. It takes nine hours, and the woman with the peewee photo cries.

choices.label: Keep the line moving kindly
choices.result: The line, kept moving, with every name said back to them. It's efficient and warm, and you finish on time.

choices.label: Do one day
choices.result: One day of signing, and the other at the hotel pool. The organizers are gracious, and you come home rested.

scenarios.title: The Mountain Trip
scenarios.text: Friends from college plan a climbing trip for the offseason: a real mountain, ropes, a guide. Your contract has a clause about 'dangerous activities', and you've just reread it.

choices.label: Read the clause and pass
choices.result: The clause wins: you stay home and see the pictures from the summit. It's the right call, and you feel old for a week.

choices.label: Go and hike instead
choices.result: You go along, and hike the trails while they climb. You're there for the campfire and the stories, and nobody's contract is in danger.

choices.label: Go and climb
choices.result: You go and climb, and it's amazing. You don't tell your agent, and every time your ankle twinges in camp you wonder if anyone knows.

scenarios.title: The Off-Season Job Offer
scenarios.text: A company offers you an offseason job in sales: real work, a real desk, a real quota. It would be good to know you can do something other than kick.

choices.label: Take the job
choices.result: The job, taken, with a desk and a badge. You learn you're good at it, and the quota board has your name at the top by June.

choices.label: Shadow for a week
choices.result: Seven days of shadowing a top salesperson. It's useful and humbling, and you leave with a much better idea of life after football.

choices.label: Keep the offseason for your leg
choices.result: Your leg needs the offseason, you decide, and you pass. It's sensible, and you wonder about the desk all summer.

scenarios.title: Family Reunion, Pro Edition
scenarios.text: The family reunion, at a lake. Everyone wants a photo with you, an aunt wants your autograph for her mail carrier, and one uncle wants a loan for a boat.

choices.label: Take every photo
choices.result: Every photo, every autograph, and a promise to the uncle that you'll think about it. It's exhausting and warm, and {parent} beams all day.

choices.label: Say no to the loan kindly
choices.result: No to the boat, kindly and clearly. The uncle sulks through dessert, and three cousins thank you privately for saying it.

choices.label: Leave early
choices.result: An early exit, before the speeches. You'll see everyone next time, and {sibling} texts you a photo of the uncle's face.

scenarios.title: The Kicker You Grew Up Watching
scenarios.text: The kicker whose poster hung above your bed when you were ten is at your game, in a suite, and he sends word that he'd like to meet you after.

choices.label: Meet him
choices.result: A meeting in the tunnel after the game. You tell him about the poster, he laughs, and he signs your shoe like you're the fan.

choices.label: Ask him everything
choices.result: How did he last so long, through all of it? You ask him everything, for an hour in the tunnel, and he answers every question honestly.

choices.label: Shake his hand
choices.result: A handshake and a simple thank-you, nothing more. It's brief, and it's enough, and you call {parent} from the car on the way home.

scenarios.title: The Rule Change
scenarios.text: The league moves the extra-point line back again, the second time in your career. The young kickers in camp are thrilled about it; you've lived through this once already.

choices.label: Adjust your training
choices.result: New distances, added to every practice the next morning. By camp the new line feels normal, and the young kickers are surprised.

choices.label: Study the change
choices.result: The change, studied properly: the angles, the wind off each end zone, the hash marks. You find the edge before anyone else in the league does.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.result: Wait until camp, you decide, and see how it feels with real snaps. It feels fine, and you're glad you didn't spend the summer worrying.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Wears Your Number
scenarios.text: A rookie at another club wears your number and tells a reporter you're the reason he started kicking. The clip is everywhere by morning, and your phone won't stop.

choices.label: Call him
choices.result: Your call reaches him on his cell, and he's speechless for ten full seconds. You wish him luck, and he calls you every season after.

choices.label: Send him a note
choices.result: The best advice you ever got, written on a card and mailed to his locker. He tapes it inside, he says, forever.

choices.label: Smile and keep it
choices.result: A smile, kept to yourself, and the clip watched twice. You don't reach out, and it stays with you all week.

scenarios.title: The Coach You Outlasted
scenarios.text: The head coach who drafted you is fired after a bad season, in a short statement on a Monday. You've outlasted him. It doesn't feel like a win at all.

choices.label: Call him
choices.result: You call him that night. He thanks you for calling, talks about your rookie camp for twenty minutes, and you hear his family in the background.

choices.label: Steady the room
choices.result: You steady the room the next morning, before the rumors start. The new coach hears about it before you meet him.

choices.label: Keep going
choices.result: You keep going, because that's the business, and you've seen it before. You keep his old playbook on a shelf at home, though.

scenarios.title: Ten Years
scenarios.text: Ten years in the league. The pension kicks in, the club gives you a watch, and the question arrives with it, uninvited: how many more?

choices.label: Go for more
choices.result: Not done, not close. You tell {coach} and your agent the same thing, and you start the eleventh year angrier than the first.

choices.label: Plan the next five years
choices.result: The next five years, planned with your agent and your family at the kitchen table. Everyone breathes easier, including you.

choices.label: Celebrate with the people who got you here
choices.result: A party for everyone who got you here: coaches, holders, {parent}, {best_friend}. The watch goes around the room twice, and {parent} cries.

scenarios.title: The Room Starts Looking at You
scenarios.text: Teammates have started bringing their problems to your locker: contracts, girlfriends, coaches, homesick kids, a lineman's divorce. You're not sure when you became that person.

choices.label: Make time
choices.result: You make time for every one of them, even when it costs you film work. You're more tired, and the room is steadier for it.

choices.label: Listen
choices.result: Mostly, you listen. It turns out that's what they need, and the young ones start bringing you coffee as a kind of payment.

choices.label: Set limits
choices.result: You set limits: after practice, never before. A few people take it personally, and you keep enough of yourself to do the job.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Staff Meeting
scenarios.text: A new coach wants to change the preparation routine that got you here: a new warmup, a new film schedule, and a new word for 'hold' that nobody can pronounce.

choices.label: Explain the routine
choices.result: Every piece of your routine, explained with reasons. He keeps most of it, changes the film schedule, and drops the new word entirely.

choices.label: Try it his way
choices.result: His way, for a month, honestly. Some of it sticks, and the coaches notice that the veteran didn't fight them.

choices.label: Find the middle over lunch
choices.result: The middle ground, found over lunch at a diner. It's mostly your routine, with his film schedule, and you both claim victory.

scenarios.title: The Family Schedule
scenarios.text: Your kids' games and your schedule are in a war you keep losing: soccer on Saturdays, recitals on Thursdays, and a road trip every other weekend of the fall.

choices.label: Make every game you can
choices.result: Every game you can make, even if it means a red-eye and a nap in the car. The kids look for you in the stands, and find you more often than not.

choices.label: Plan the season on one calendar
choices.result: One big calendar on the kitchen wall, with every game, recital and road trip in different colors. It's chaos made visible, and it helps.

choices.label: Watch the videos after practice
choices.result: The videos, watched in the locker room after practice, every one. It's not the same, and the kids know it, and they send them anyway.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Plan
scenarios.text: You sit down at the kitchen table with a calculator and a yellow pad and try to work out how much you'll need after football. The number is bigger than you expected.

choices.label: Do the math
choices.result: The math, done properly with an honest advisor over three meetings. It's sobering and useful, and you finally know what 'enough' looks like.

choices.label: Do it with {love_interest}
choices.result: {parent} sits beside you with a second calculator and decades of experience. You make the plan together, and it's better for it.

choices.label: Leave it for next year
choices.result: Next year, you decide, and the yellow pad goes in a drawer. The number keeps growing in your head anyway.
